label.explanation: Mecho Autotech sells on-demand vehicle repair, servicing, and spare-part booking through an app and a network of vetted mechanics, mainly to individual vehicle owners in Africa, which places it in consumer vehicle-ownership services.

Wibond sells buy-now-pay-later installment credit to underbanked Latin American consumers without credit cards, delivered as a checkout payment method that it integrates into online merchants' purchase flows.

Green Canopy NODE manufactures flat-pack prefab house assembly kits and construction software that it deploys through its own residential pipeline as a vertically integrated developer, general contractor and real estate fund manager. This places it primarily in construction technology, with a genuine secondary role in housing development.

Peakflo sells agentic workflow software with ERP integrations to business finance teams, automating accounts receivable (invoice-to-cash), accounts payable (procure-to-pay), and expense reimbursement, with some broader back-office operations automation.

Junction Bioscience uses an autonomous AI hypothesis engine to discover molecules, but it applies that engine to its own pipeline of therapies for neuroinflammatory and immune diseases rather than selling it, so it is primarily a therapeutics developer with a strong drug-discovery platform component.

Polar sells USD deposit accounts and currency exchange (including stablecoin withdrawals) to non-U.S. remote workers, freelancers, and online sellers so they can hold dollar earnings and convert them to local currency more cheaply, with a secondary fit in cross-border money transfer.

Belvo sells an open-finance API, a "Plaid for Latam," that lets fintechs, companies and developers access and interpret their end-users' bank and financial data, which makes it core financial-data infrastructure with a secondary fit as a developer-facing API product.

Educato sells AI-generated exam-prep content and platforms directly to students worldwide preparing for underserved standardized and professional exams, which is fundamentally an education business; a secondary fit is consumer career services, since many of these exams gate professional advancement.

Buoyant Aero builds and operates zero-emissions autonomous drone blimps that it sells as an aerial advertising medium to businesses seeking to reach audiences in new locations, combining unmanned aerial vehicle technology with an out-of-home marketing service.

Candor sells AI agents that find and pursue government contracts and grants for defense and deeptech companies, which makes it a business-development and capture tool that wins revenue from government buyers.

UrbanKisaan sells plant-biology foundation models (genome variant ranking, genotype-to-phenotype prediction, geospatial crop mapping) and autonomous speed-breeding growth chambers to seed breeders, agribusinesses, and growers to compress crop variety development, which places it squarely in agriculture with a secondary fit in automated controlled-environment hardware.

Skymerse sells AI software for airline flight operations, covering operations-center planning and monitoring and real-time cockpit support (starting with its Notamify NOTAM product), to airlines, pilots and aviation professionals; this places it in aviation, with secondary fit as operations workflow software.

Wren sells monthly carbon-offset subscriptions, funding nature, industry, and policy projects, plus footprint-reduction guidance, directly to individual consumers; the product is climate mitigation, but the buyers are households rather than corporate customers.

PNOĒ sells a clinical-grade breath-analysis (metabolic/VO2max) device with software and expert support to health professionals, longevity clinics, and fitness providers, who use it to measure clients' physiology and prescribe personalized nutrition, exercise, and bio-optimization programs aimed at wellness rather than clinical treatment.

Code Four sells AI software to police departments that turns body camera footage into reports and connects with records and evidence systems, which makes it government-focused workflow automation with a secondary fit in B2B operations software.

Abalone Bio is developing its own activating antibody drugs for obesity and metabolic disease, which it intends to take to patients, and it also licenses its high-throughput, ML-driven GPCR antibody discovery platform to pharma partners.

LineLeap sells line-skip passes, drinks, cover, and event tickets to consumers at nightlife venues through its mobile app, and it gives those bars and venues commerce and customer-marketing tools to generate new revenue.
Star sells an AI-powered no-code game creation tool to individual creators and aspiring game makers, placing it in consumer gaming, with a secondary fit as a product-building and design tool.

Soteri Skin sells non-prescription skincare products direct to consumers, aimed at relief for people with chronic skin conditions like eczema and psoriasis, which places it in consumer cosmetics with a secondary self-directed health and wellness angle.

Canix sells compliance and operations management software to cannabis businesses, covering their cultivation, processing, and distribution workflows; it is primarily a back-office operations tool, with a secondary fit in cultivation and grow management for growers.

Elevate sells FDIC-insured US-based USD deposit accounts with debit cards and low-cost cross-border payouts to non-US residents in emerging markets who need to get paid in dollars, making it primarily a banking product with a secondary money-transfer component.

Bemlo sells AI-driven scheduling and workforce management software to healthcare and social care provider organizations to manage staffing operations, making it healthcare operational IT with a strong HR/workforce-management angle.

Bild AI sells AI software to Division 8 door, frame, and hardware contractors and suppliers that reads blueprints and specs to automate takeoff, opening schedules, and bid pricing for construction projects.

Ten Lives uses AI to optimize engineered microbial factories that produce low-cost, sustainable proteins, likely including pet food given the 'all members of the family' framing. That makes it a non-therapeutic biomanufacturing business selling to food producers, with a secondary fit in food production.

TwentyTwo builds AI-powered biosecurity infrastructure, a defensive stack against engineered pandemics, most likely sold to government and security customers as biothreat countermeasure technology; it may also involve pathogen detection, though its exact product and buyers aren't stated.

Gauss sells consumers an AI credit agent that refinances expensive credit card debt using an instantly originated line of credit, making it primarily a consumer lending product with a secondary role in personal financial management.

Vitable Health sells startups and SMBs an employee health benefit, ICHRA administration bundled with direct primary care (virtual visits, prescriptions, labs) delivered by its own clinicians, so it is both a care-delivery service and an employer benefits platform.

Olio Labs develops its own AI-discovered combination drug therapies, led by obesity treatments, for regulatory approval and use in patients; its custom ML platform for searching drug combinations also places it in AI-driven drug discovery.

Astor sells an AI investment advisor that surfaces opportunities and delivers personalized analysis to retail investors, making it an investment decision-making and wealth advisory tool for individuals.

MaverickX sells specialty chemical solutions (PetroX and LithX) to oil producers and mining operators to improve recovery of oil from shale reservoirs and metals such as lithium from low-grade ores, which best fits Industrials/Energy since the schema has no dedicated mining or chemicals category.

Tranqui sells ML-driven digital debt collection to Latin American creditors, a back-end service in the lending lifecycle, and it also gives indebted consumers personalized repayment plans to improve their financial health.

Lygg develops a patented, photostable UVA-filtering ingredient that it sells to skincare and sunscreen brands to improve anti-aging sun protection; because US sunscreen actives are FDA-regulated drug compounds requiring approval, it also fits Therapeutics as a secondary label.

Splash builds low-cost autonomous surface patrol vessels for national security customers to defend critical maritime assets like oil rigs and shipping terminals, which places it squarely in defense, with a secondary fit in autonomous robotics and mass manufacturing.

TovenAI sells AI agents that automate manual, data-intensive regulatory compliance work to compliance teams at institutional trading firms and brokerages, which fits Fintech's compliance software for financial institutions.

Cardamon sells an AI regulatory-compliance platform to regulated financial firms, used by their compliance officers and product teams to turn financial regulation into obligations and product requirements, which matches compliance software for financial institutions, with a secondary fit as regulatory and legal workflow tooling.
Vinci Games develops and sells multiplayer VR games like Blacktop Hoops and Ruffnauts directly to consumer players on Meta Quest; the core value is gameplay, delivered on an immersive VR platform.

Ontra Mobility sells data-driven planning and real-time optimization software to cities and transit agencies to improve ground transit service and ridership, as in the on-demand systems MARTA Reach and CAT SMART.

PrimeVault sells digital asset and stablecoin infrastructure (custody wallets, programmable treasury, compliance, and market access) to enterprises and financial institutions, fitting crypto custody and exchange infrastructure, with a secondary fit in Payments for moving stablecoins.
OlaClick sells digital menu, WhatsApp ordering, POS, and CRM/marketing software to mass-market restaurants in Latin America to manage and grow their consumer-facing commerce.

FrontPage sells a social community platform to individual Indian retail traders and investors, where the core value is connecting with peers to share trading ideas and learn from one another, with secondary relevance to investment decision-making.

Tokenless sells research services and tooling to AI labs and ML teams that train models with RL, build environments, or run agent evals, helping them detect and fix reward hacking and other environment and eval flaws, which makes it a developer-facing tool for building AI products.

Kingdom uses AI to discover and develop clinically validated microbial (Superculture) ingredients, which it sells to pet and human health product makers as non-therapeutic bio-based inputs for wellness products.

EduRev sells an education and learning app, a 'Netflix for Education' with course content and social features, directly to Indian students, so it fits the Education domain under Other, with a secondary fit as consumer content.

Hadrius sells an AI platform that consolidates and automates securities regulatory compliance for regulated financial firms such as investment advisers, which best matches compliance software for financial institutions, with a secondary fit as regulatory and legal compliance tooling.

Univerbal sells an AI-powered conversational language-learning app with a personal AI tutor directly to individual learners, which is consumer education and fits the Other domain rather than any of the listed industry subcategories.

PowerUs runs a job marketplace that helps skilled blue-collar workers like electricians and mechanics find better-paying full-time jobs, and it also serves as a hiring channel for the employers recruiting them.

Vorticity sells a high-performance scientific computing platform, built from custom processor architecture and system design, that lets engineers in energy, aerospace and life sciences simulate designs before building them, so it fits industrial engineering software with a secondary fit as compute infrastructure.

CentralComs sells AI agents that run call intake, technician dispatch, and customer updates for home services businesses inside their existing field-service software. That is operational workflow automation for those businesses; capturing inbound leads and booking jobs is a secondary sales angle.

Homebase sells rent-to-own home financing, an alternative to high-interest mortgages, to aspiring homebuyers in Southeast Asia, making it primarily a consumer lending business with a strong residential real estate component.

FlatX sells an AI-powered rental marketplace that helps young urban renters in India find flats without brokers. Its flatmate-matching feature, which connects renters with each other, also gives it a social-consumer angle.

GroundControl sells AI software to manufacturers in highly-regulated industries, starting with aerospace parts suppliers, that automates the quality documentation required for every manufactured part.

Permitify sells an AI co-pilot to city building departments, helping their plan reviewers check building plans for code compliance and issue permits faster, which places it in construction plan review and inspection tooling with a government buyer.

Mass Magnetics makes domestically produced permanent magnets from recycled rare-earth scrap and sells them to robotics, industrial, aerospace, and defense manufacturers for use in motors, sensors, and electronics, with DFARS compliance making defense a key secondary market.

Conntour sells AI software that lets organizations search footage, set real-time alerts, and extract data from thousands of security cameras using natural language, a physical-security threat-detection tool with clear surveillance use for government and defense customers.

Mayflower sells an AI plug-in to company HR teams that screens global candidates for immigration eligibility, classifies visa pathways, and produces attorney-ready forms, streamlining compliant international hiring with a secondary legal-compliance angle.

Upstream sells an AI email assistant that sorts, drafts replies, follows up, and handles inbox tasks like scheduling for individual professionals and teams, making it a general-purpose productivity tool rather than software for a specific department.

Birch Biosciences sells an engineered-enzyme, synthetic-biology recycling process to plastic manufacturers and recyclers, breaking polymers down into chemical building blocks, which is a non-therapeutic industrial bio application whose main pitch is a 70% cut in carbon emissions.

DigiBuild sells an LLM-powered procurement and materials-tracking platform to general contractors, subcontractors, and real estate developers to find, order, and manage building materials from supplier to job site, making it construction software with a strong supply-chain component.

Reframe sells a neuroscience- and psychology-based mobile app directly to individual consumers to help them quit or cut back on drinking, which is self-directed wellness and habit change rather than provider-led clinical treatment.

Morada Uno sells tenant screening, rent collection, and lease insurance (a replacement for property-owning guarantors) to landlords, brokers, and tenants in Latin America, making it primarily a rental-insurance underwriter serving the residential real estate market.

BluumBio sells engineered bacteria, plants, enzymes and bioreactor systems to industrial and environmental customers that break down toxic chemicals for pollution remediation, a non-therapeutic engineered-organism application.

Paces sells AI agents, software, and diligence services to renewable energy and data center developers. These tools automate siting, interconnection, and permitting so power projects reach construction-ready status faster, which places it primarily in energy infrastructure with a secondary fit in pre-construction development.

Medium Biosciences uses AI protein design to make experimentally validated affinity reagents, the binding molecules at the core of assays, for diagnostic developers and life-science research teams; its AI design platform for research customers also fits drug discovery tooling.

Wanderlog sells a collaborative trip-planning app to individual travelers. It helps them research destinations, organize itineraries, map routes, and book hotels, which places it squarely in consumer travel planning.

BuildJet sells a compute cloud built on gaming CPUs to software engineering teams, offering faster, cheaper drop-in runners for GitHub Actions CI. That makes it core compute infrastructure that also functions as a developer tool.

Nano sells an earned-wage, daily-pay app to retailers and manufacturers in Southeast Asia that plugs into their HRM and attendance systems to cut turnover and boost engagement, while giving hourly workers faster access to their pay.

Sensei sells human-demonstration training data collection, enabled by its low-cost hardware and a network of paid operators, to robotics companies building and training robot models, functioning as a data-infrastructure supplier to the robotics industry.

Junction sells a developer API to health tech companies that unifies wearable-device data and at-home lab test kit fulfillment, making it health data infrastructure for healthcare businesses rather than a direct care or diagnostic product.

Tough Commerce sells a white-label commerce platform to construction material suppliers, producers, and manufacturers. It digitizes their ordering, dispatching, delivery, e-ticketing, invoicing, and payments, so it is construction-specific software with a significant logistics component.

Clear offers consumers a free skincare app for tracking routines, products and selfies with brand-agnostic product recommendations, and builds a skin-outcomes dataset for brands and clinicians, which places it in consumer beauty with a self-directed skin-health wellness angle.

Envelope sells a personal budgeting app to individual consumers, helping them plan and control everyday spending, and it has built-in checking accounts and debit cards, which adds a consumer banking component.

Foundation sells an online buyer-experience and sales platform to homebuilders, letting them market and sell new homes to homebuyers and handle purchase and ownership online, which makes it primarily a residential property sales tool with secondary ties to builders' construction operations.

Tank Payments sells payables automation software to logistics businesses that pay trucking carriers, which is payment facilitation, and it also offers a banking platform to the trucking businesses themselves.

Glen sells companies a shared memory and context layer that collects agent sessions, code, tickets, and docs and injects relevant institutional context into coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor, which makes it context-handling infrastructure that engineering teams build their agent workflows on.

Maywood sells a finance-compliant, always-on AI assistant to investment bankers and private-market dealmakers that tracks relationships and pipeline, flags origination opportunities, drafts outreach, updates CRMs, and prepares meeting briefs, which is mainly deal-pipeline and relationship-driven selling software built for financial firms.

Stable sells startups and other businesses a virtual business address and digital mailroom service, which falls under office logistics. The service lets them view, forward, and shred mail remotely and guides them through compliant address changes.
Lucid Bots sells cleaning drones and a ground-based pressure-washing robot to commercial cleaning businesses and property operators, automating dull, dirty, and dangerous exterior cleaning work.

Nori manufactures and sells a low-cost general-purpose humanoid mobile manipulator robot to both businesses and households for automating physical tasks like cleaning, restocking, and folding clothes, placing it in robotics with a meaningful consumer hardware angle.

peopleCQ (NowPay) offers employees in Egypt and other emerging markets an employer-backed financial-wellness benefit, centered on on-demand salary advances plus bill pay and budgeting tools, so it fits Consumer Finance, with a secondary Credit and Lending fit because the advances are a form of credit.

Lizza sells an AI assistant to D2C e-commerce brands that finds, contacts, and manages influencer and creator partnerships, which is a customer-acquisition marketing tool, while also giving content creators a way to earn a living from brand deals.

Abatable sells a carbon offset procurement platform that provides project quality assessments, standardized multi-year purchase agreements, and automated RFPs, connecting corporate buyers with carbon project developers so they can mitigate their climate impact.

Ansa sells enzymatically synthesized DNA, a research tool for biotech and pharmaceutical researchers developing therapeutics, diagnostics, and biomanufacturing products, so it fits best as drug-discovery infrastructure, with a secondary fit in industrial bio because its synthetic DNA also supports biomanufacturing.

Vision Lab sells structured first-person factory video and SOP-level process data to robotics and AI labs so they can train robots on real industrial production workflows, which makes it a data infrastructure provider for the manufacturing and robotics sector.

Cash Flow Portal sells investment management software to real estate syndicators for raising capital, handling subscription documents and wire instructions, and managing their investors, which makes it fund and asset management tooling applied to real estate deals.

Cardinal Gray sells LLM-powered lending infrastructure to auto lenders, automating DMV lien filings and title work across states and counties, so it fits as lending automation for financial institutions with an automotive-finance angle.

Rarebird sells coffee made with paraxanthine, a caffeine replacement, directly to caffeine-sensitive consumers, so it is a consumer beverage product with a secondary wellness angle around reducing anxiety and jitteriness.

Moneco sells neobank current accounts and payment cards to African migrants living in Europe, with free remittances as a money-transfer feature, making deposit banking its core and cross-border payments a genuine secondary line.

Slicker sells AI-powered payment retry and failed-payment recovery software to subscription businesses, helping them reduce involuntary churn and turn past-due recurring payments into collected revenue.

FLOWER CO. is a vertically integrated legal cannabis company that sells cannabis online to individual consumers, with next-day delivery to homes across California, so it fits best as consumer convenience delivery; cannabis edibles are a secondary fit.

Community Phone sells a no-setup phone, AI-powered check-in calls, and a companion family app directly to seniors and their families, so families can keep watch over the wellbeing of aging parents living at home.

Bloom sells individual American consumers an investing app and long-term wealth-building brokerage account, bundled with gamified financial-education lessons, so it is primarily a retail investment platform with a strong consumer financial-literacy component.

Littio sells USD-denominated savings accounts, a Mastercard debit card, and dollar investing options directly to Latin American consumers, acting as a neobank that holds and converts deposits so customers avoid local currency devaluation.

Epsilon3 sells AI-powered ERP, MES, and test-management SaaS to manufacturers and operators of complex engineered systems, with a strong focus on aerospace and space missions as well as energy, defense, and maritime customers.

Shinkei Systems sells robotic systems that automate traditional ikejime fish-harvesting techniques to fish farmers and harvesters. Its customers are food producers improving seafood quality and shelf-life, which makes Agriculture the primary fit; the core technology is robotics, which is why Manufacturing and Robotics is the secondary pick.

Plena sells AI software to specialty medical practices that automates administrative workflows such as referrals, fax intake, scheduling, procedure compliance, and collections, which makes it healthcare IT for providers rather than clinical care.

SureBright sells an AI-powered extended-warranty platform that e-commerce merchants embed in their checkout. It uses LLMs to match and price product protection policies, which makes it fundamentally insurance underwriting and distribution tech, delivered as a retail commerce tool.

Zephyr Fusion is building a megawatt-class in-orbit fusion reactor to supply power to commercial and government operators running large-scale industry in space, making it chiefly a power-generation company with a strong space-infrastructure component.

Hop Aero builds hypersonic point-to-point rocket cargo vehicles that deliver supplies into contested environments for the U.S. military and allies, making it primarily a defense company whose core technology is rocketry and aerospace.

Alguna sells B2B SaaS companies a quote-to-cash platform whose core is billing, invoicing, and payment collection for finance teams, with CPQ deal-quoting tools that also serve sales and revenue operations.

Interfaze sells developers and product teams an AI model, accessed via API, that combines specialized DNN/CNN models with transformers to give consistent, deterministic output for document intelligence, object detection, classification and audio tasks inside their software, and as a foundational model layer it also fits AI infrastructure.

Mailwarm sells email deliverability tools (warmup, diagnostics, and managed deliverability services) to businesses running email marketing and cold outreach, so their messages reach the inbox instead of spam.

marketfeed sells personal financial guidance and money-management products directly to individual Indian consumers to diagnose and fix their finances, with an investing and trading heritage that also touches retail asset management.

Flick sells end-to-end AI filmmaking software, a 'Figma for AI filmmaking', to independent creators and filmmakers, and also produces its own AI films and template content for its community, which places it closest to media and content creation; it also serves as a creative productivity tool for professional film teams.

KubeSail sells Kubernetes-based self-hosting and on-demand software deployment infrastructure, used by companies like ChatWoot to spin up customer instances, and also sells PiBox home-hosting hardware that lets individual consumers run apps at home.

Benepass sells HR teams a benefits-administration platform that consolidates tax-advantaged accounts and company-funded stipends for employees, delivered via a single card and app built on its own payments stack.

Cocreate sells video production workflow software to film and TV professionals such as editors, DITs, post supervisors, and UPMs, automating tedious tasks like footage organization, slating, and timecode and script note management so they work faster.

o11 sells an AI-maintained data warehouse to financial firms such as investment and deal-focused shops; it unifies CRM, email, data rooms, and market data into a secure, agent-ready model for deal, relationship, and business intelligence.

Innate sells general-purpose personal AI robots, open hardware platforms that individuals and developers can teach with code, language and demonstrations, so it is primarily a consumer hardware device company that also operates in general robotics.
Metreecs sells AI demand-forecasting software to retailers to plan, buy, and allocate inventory, preventing overstock and stockouts, which also touches supply chain inventory management.

Alga Biosciences sells a biology-based feed product to the cattle industry that cuts enteric methane emissions from cows, so it is primarily a climate-mitigation product with a livestock-agriculture customer base.

ValCtrl sells individual traders a prediction-market venue that turns any user-typed, resolvable belief into a priced, tradable event contract, with ValCtrl itself taking the other side under risk and compliance controls; this is exchange and trading infrastructure, with a secondary fit as consumer wagering on outcomes.

xPay sells international payment acceptance and remittance infrastructure to SaaS businesses with overseas customers, along with billing operations like invoicing, reconciliation and foreign sales tax compliance that also place it in B2B finance and accounting.

Serif Health sells healthcare price-transparency data products and APIs that ingest and organize payer and provider pricing and reimbursement data, giving healthcare organizations a data layer for contracting and cost analysis.

Arpeggio Bio develops its own drugs against transcription factors, with a lead program for IO-resistant melanoma headed to patients, and it also offers its AI and high-throughput RNA-sequencing discovery platform to pharma partners like J&J and FORMA.

Dreamscale Labs sells a low-latency cloud inference platform to robotics companies and engineering teams, letting them run their physical AI models in the cloud instead of on expensive on-robot GPUs, which makes it compute infrastructure serving the robotics industry.

WANTD runs a mobile-first consumer marketplace (live commerce, auctions, influencer network) where fashion and footwear brands sell directly to shoppers. It also gives those brands storefront-alternative sales channels and fulfillment, which justifies the B2B Retail secondary.

Palmier sells an open-source AI-native video editor that lets agents like Claude and Codex trim, reorder, and generate footage, a general-purpose creative tool for creators and teams; its showcase use, making cinematic launch videos for startups, also places it in marketing content production.

Lumeria sells individual consumers a phone-clip multispectral skin-scanning camera and companion software that tracks skin changes over time, links flare-ups to their causes, and recommends products, offering self-directed skin-health insight rather than clinical diagnosis.

Cinder sells trust-and-safety infrastructure to businesses, from frontier AI labs to e-commerce and social platforms, to detect, investigate, and mitigate abuse, content harms, and AI misuse, with secondary fit as operations workflow tooling for moderation teams.

Bayesline sells a GPU-powered, cloud-deployed financial analytics suite to institutional investors like hedge funds and asset managers so they can build custom risk and portfolio analytics that support investment decisions, making it primarily an asset-management tool with a strong analytics-software character.

Hamming AI sells a testing and production-monitoring platform to voice AI product and engineering teams, letting them auto-generate test calls before deployment and track live calls with built-in metrics and alerts.

EARTH AI uses predictive AI and its own low-disturbance drilling technology to discover and test critical metal deposits, then supplies them to the mining and resource sector behind the energy transition; mining has no dedicated subindustry, so Industrials/Energy is the closest fit.
Aviron sells connected exercise machines (rowers and similar hardware) directly to individual consumers, paired with an immersive gaming platform that gamifies at-home workouts.

Shimmer sells affordable one-on-one, human-delivered ADHD coaching directly to individuals with ADHD or executive function challenges, making it a people-performed support service that is also sold direct-to-consumer as non-clinical wellness and self-improvement.

Gojiberry sells AI go-to-market agents to B2B companies that replace SDRs and agencies by finding intent-showing buyers, running outbound outreach, handling replies, and booking qualified meetings, which is primarily outbound sales with overlap into lead generation.

Clad sells project management, billing, payments, and permitting software to contractors, utilities, and internet operators who build physical infrastructure like power and telecom networks, which places it squarely in construction software with an energy-grid buildout angle.

Hebbian Robotics sells developer-facing data infrastructure that lets physical AI and robotics teams build automated data-evaluation and quality-control pipelines with fast, cheap custom models, so it is primarily B2B ML data infrastructure that serves the robotics industry.

Leadbay sells AI-driven lead discovery and qualification software to B2B go-to-market teams, such as those at L'Oréal and Saint-Gobain, to expand their addressable market and feed qualified prospects into sales and agentic outbound workflows; it also overlaps with lead generation for marketing.

Invertix sells custom physics-informed AI models to energy and critical-infrastructure operators that ingest SCADA and operational data to run their plants and grids more efficiently, which squarely fits energy management for utilities and industrial operators, with a secondary fit as industrial automation software.

Stipop sells a Patreon-style platform that lets independent character IP creators earn revenue directly from fans who buy and engage with their character content, and it also sells a sticker API and SDK to chat apps and software companies.

Valence sells systematic traders trading infrastructure that aggregates and executes contracts across prediction-market exchanges like Kalshi and Polymarket, which fits Banking and Exchange; its arbitrage detection, API, and backtesting tools for building data-driven strategies also make Asset Management a genuine secondary fit.

MedCrypt sells a cybersecurity toolkit and ML-based threat detection network to medical device manufacturers, helping them secure connected devices and meet security regulations, making it a security product serving the healthcare device sector.
Bidflow sells AI takeoff and estimating software to electrical contractors, using vision models to count symbols in CAD drawings so they can submit competitive construction bids faster.

Kivo Health delivers AI-powered virtual care for seniors with chronic lung disease, working with health systems such as Stanford, UCLA and Optum Health and with payers to keep patients out of the hospital; it is primarily a care delivery service, with an AI software layer as a secondary fit.

Machine26 runs a marketplace, supported by an inspection app, that lets construction companies and other machine owners sell used construction equipment to international used-equipment dealers; it secondarily fits wholesale distribution of physical goods.

Consus sells a compliant AI-routing API and managed infrastructure that lets aerospace and defense companies use the latest AI models on ITAR/CUI-controlled data without handling the compliance paperwork or backend engineering themselves.

Verdant sells AI agents to local governments to automate internal workflows, starting with building permit review, so it is govtech (Other) whose initial wedge sits in the construction permitting and inspection process.

Manara sells access to vetted Middle East and North Africa software engineering talent to global tech companies for hiring, while also giving the engineers themselves interview preparation and job referrals.

Volopay sells corporate cards, domestic and cross-border bill payments, and spend management software to Southeast Asian businesses' finance and accounting teams, making it primarily a business payments company with a secondary fit in finance and accounting tooling.

DocVita sells telehealth care delivery to patients in India, with human concierges coordinating appointments in 11 local languages and handling back-office work for doctors, making it a people-driven care service.

AveryIQ sells AI leasing and property-management agents to property managers and landlords, helping them fill vacancies, schedule tours, and resolve tenant maintenance requests on already-built rental properties; its two-way tenant contact center also makes it a customer-support operations tool.

Libra Robotics sells AI-coordinated robotic crews that align, fasten, and install components to builders and developers of large infrastructure projects such as utility-scale solar farms and data centers, combining industrial robotics with construction automation.

Propaya sells an AI platform to commercial real estate owners, property managers, and legal teams that extracts lease terms, obligations, and property-risk signals from documents to manage existing property portfolios, with secondary overlap in legal lease and contract review.

Blueshoe is an AI-native, full-stack consumer and plaintiff law firm that sells legal guidance and representation directly to individuals. That makes it a consumer personal-services business (which the taxonomy says includes legal help for individuals), not B2B legal software sold to companies or law firms.

Udhaar sells a mobile bookkeeping and credit-ledger app to Pakistan's micro SMEs so they can digitally track store credit, sales, and cash, with a likely extension into payments and money flow for those merchants.

The Context Company sells conversation-analytics software that mines every customer interaction with a production AI agent for account-level patterns of churn, cost, and unmet needs, aimed at engineering, product, and customer-success teams; its IDE/MCP integration, trace-level debugging, and before-and-after benchmarking also make it a developer tool for shipping agent fixes.

Elimentary sells AI agents to private capital managers that autonomously run post-investment middle- and back-office fund operations, such as NAV calculations. It starts with structured credit workflows like borrowing base calculations and loan tape processing, which also places it in lending infrastructure automation.

Tinfoil sells developers and companies a confidential-computing platform (a private inference API, SDKs, and secure-enclave containers on NVIDIA GPUs) that encrypts AI workloads and verifiably keeps data private even from the cloud provider, so its core value is data protection, delivered as compute infrastructure that teams build on.

Future Fields sells contract biomanufacturing of hard-to-produce recombinant proteins to biotech, life sciences, and pharma companies, using a multicellular engineered-organism platform, which makes it primarily an industrial bio play that also supplies inputs to drug development.

RealPact sells AI agents to real estate brokerages that pull property records and automate transaction paperwork, contracts, document organization, and deadline tracking, which makes it real estate transaction software with a secondary fit as back-office operations automation.

Axial sells GPU-native physics, geometry, and simulation kernels to engineering and manufacturing teams, making it engineering software for industrial design and production with a secondary fit as developer-facing programmable building blocks.
Toko sells an AI-powered mobile English-speaking practice app directly to language learners in East Asia, which makes it a consumer education product that falls under Other (education).

Shor sells international payroll and employer-of-record services to startup founders for hiring and paying overseas employees and contractors, with compliant contracts and same-day local-currency cross-border payouts.

Cortex AI sells real-world egocentric human video, robot trajectory data, and human-in-the-loop evaluation services to frontier labs building robotics foundation models and general-purpose robots, making it a data infrastructure provider for the robotics industry.

Kite sells a screen-recording and video-editing tool that software companies, such as YC startups, use to produce polished product demo videos for launches, social media, landing pages and feature announcements, making it mainly a marketing content tool with general-purpose productivity appeal.

BotBuilt sells robotically prefabricated house components and the robotic systems behind them to residential builders, addressing the construction labor shortage with automated, AI- and vision-driven manufacturing.
ZeroSettle sells a drop-in mobile SDK to app developers that replaces App Store in-app purchase billing with direct payment processing, cutting platform fees and enabling instant payouts.

Segmed sells access to a de-identified real-world medical imaging data network to life sciences and health-tech companies for AI model development, evidence generation, and patient recruitment, making it primarily healthcare data infrastructure with a secondary role supporting pharma research.

RendaloMaq rents heavy equipment through its tech platform (ROS) to construction and mining companies in Latin America, along with fleet-management software. That makes it primarily a construction-industry offering, with a secondary fit in industrial equipment operations.

SpruceID sells decentralized identity and digital wallet infrastructure (credential issuance, verification, and user-controlled data vaults) to governments, enterprises, and blockchain ecosystems, which they build identity and data-sharing systems on top of.

Dialogus sells self-improving AI voice agents to enterprises to run high-volume contact center workflows. Customer support is the core use, which fits Operations, while sales calls and collections give a secondary fit in Sales.

Covera sells AI agents to insurance brokerages that automate servicing workflows such as submission intake, carrier quoting, claims handling, and collections, which makes it insurance brokerage technology with a secondary fit as back-office operations automation.

Spenny sells automated round-up micro-investing into diversified portfolios, charging a fee on assets under management, to Indian millennial consumers who otherwise don't invest; its broader aim of managing everyday personal finances also fits consumer finance.

Spenmo sells accounts-payable and spend management software to business finance teams, covering bill payment, corporate cards, transfers, expense claims and automated reconciliation, so it also operates as business payments infrastructure.

Kenobi sells businesses an AI website-personalization tool that tailors landing-page content to each visitor to boost conversion, which is primarily a marketing function with some spillover into moving prospects through the sales journey.

Nectar sells an AI energy management platform and utility data API to facility and sustainability teams for analyzing utility data, optimizing energy costs, and reporting efficiency metrics, which places it in energy management with a secondary fit in climate/emissions reporting.

Portão 3 sells a Ramp-style corporate payments and spend management platform to companies in Latin America, making it primarily a business payments fintech with a secondary fit in B2B finance and accounting tooling.
Vestris sells AI software that automates title processing from contract to close for title shops, streamlining real estate transaction services within the title insurance workflow.

OnePatch sells an AI site-reliability agent to engineering teams that instruments production services, detects incidents, and drives them to shipped fixes, making it observability and on-call infrastructure that also acts as a developer tool.

Playgent sells sandbox environment infrastructure to enterprise engineering teams building AI agents. Each environment is packaged as an MCP endpoint with mocked tool calls, abstracted auth and initialized test data, so teams can reproduce production failures and export traces to observability or RL pipelines.

Probably Genetic sells a patient intelligence platform to drug developers and patient advocacy groups, using online patient discovery, machine learning, and at-home genetic testing to diagnose rare genetic disease patients and route them to clinical trials and treatments.

Daybreak Health delivers clinician-provided teletherapy and psychiatry care to youth, reaching them through partnerships with schools and pediatric groups and paid for by insurance and government funding, which makes it a people-delivered care service rather than a software or device product.

Proof of Human sells an API to online platforms that invisibly detects bots and verifies that users are human without CAPTCHAs, which is primarily a security product, with a secondary fit as a developer-facing identity verification building block.

ACX sells biological crop-protection products (biocides) to growers and agribusinesses as eco-friendly alternatives to chemical pesticides, with its bio-based approach also fitting non-therapeutic industrial biotech.

Notabene sells a SaaS compliance platform to crypto businesses such as exchanges and VASPs, letting them run counterparty due diligence and meet bank-like regulations like the Travel Rule. That fits crypto compliance infrastructure, and its role as a SWIFT-like network for screening transfers also touches payments.

Impossible Metals builds underwater robotic vehicles that harvest polymetallic nodules from the seabed, producing battery metals (nickel, cobalt, manganese, copper) sold under off-take agreements to industrial buyers in the EV and battery supply chain, so its core is robotics with a secondary fit in the energy and battery materials value chain.

Ancana sells fractional co-ownership shares in fully managed vacation homes to individual buyers, handling the ownership structuring, co-owner matching, and property management, with a leisure-travel component through usage weeks, rentals, and stay swaps.

Swadesh sells a bundled neobank offering to newly arrived Indian immigrants in the US: a free FDIC-insured checking account, a credit-building card, cheaper remittances and SIM plans, plus add-ons like insurance and housing help. Because it serves an underserved demographic's everyday financial life, Consumer Finance fits best, with deposit-account banking as a genuine secondary.

Taiga sells AI software to doctor's offices that automates medical coding, claim scrubbing, insurance submission, and denial management, which is a revenue-cycle administrative workflow for healthcare providers.
HyLight builds and operates unmanned drone-airship hybrids that sell inspection services to energy and infrastructure operators, detecting pipeline methane leaks and power-line and railway defects.

Goldbridge sells an AI-powered banking and financial operations platform (deposit accounts, reserve yield, and expense management) to real estate owners and landlords, putting it primarily in fintech banking with a strong real estate vertical focus.
MICSI sells AI software to imaging centers that doubles MRI resolution and halves scan time, enhancing diagnostic imaging quality and throughput toward quantitative, reproducible diagnoses.

Albiware sells an all-in-one SaaS platform (CRM, project management, field documentation, scheduling, BI) to insurance damage repair contractors to run their restoration jobs and streamline claims documentation and payment.

Pools sells a memberships platform to arts, music, and cultural event organizers that upsells ticket buyers into memberships at checkout, helping these organizations retain and engage their audiences.

Stellon Labs builds tiny open-source AI models such as the KittenTTS text-to-speech model, which developers and product teams embed in apps running on smartphones, wearables, and embedded devices, so it fits best as a developer-facing building block, with a secondary fit as AI infrastructure.

IronLedger sells AI-powered accounts payable automation, invoice processing, and corporate cards to property managers, developers, and contractors, which makes it a vertical finance-and-accounting tool for the real estate industry.
Lantern AI sells an AI hiring platform to companies that handles the full recruiting loop, from sourcing and screening candidates through interviews, assessments, and offers.

Topline Pro sells a generative-AI platform to home service professionals that builds SEO-optimized websites, syncs local listings, and automates social media so customers can discover and book them, which is mainly a customer-acquisition (marketing) tool with Shopify-like storefront and online-payment features.

Sidekick sells custom manufacturing shops an AI agent that runs shop-floor operations over text. It answers workers from the shop's own documents, monitors live machine data to prevent downtime, and routes work orders and purchase orders. That makes it industrial automation software for manufacturers, with a secondary fit as operations workflow software.

Lyon sells private foundation models, trained on each customer's own transaction data, to banks, insurers, and fintechs to predict credit, fraud, collections, churn, and lifetime value; credit decisioning is its headline deployment, and the product is also predictive analytics infrastructure for financial institutions.

Usul sells an AI platform that helps companies, especially defense and government contractors, find, match to, and win public-sector contracts across 60+ nations, making it a business-development and sales-pipeline tool for B2B sellers rather than a defense technology itself.

Magic Hour sells a browser-based suite of more than 100 AI tools for generating and editing video, images, and audio, used by creators and teams to produce media faster, and also offers the same capabilities to developers through a REST API, SDKs, and an MCP server.

SaveIN sells healthcare-focused financing to Indian consumers, letting them split medical and wellness bills into monthly instalments, while also connecting them with the 5,000+ partner healthcare practices that offer these payment plans.

Tandem is an AI-native office leasing brokerage that helps businesses find and lease already-built commercial office space, especially smaller and shorter-term units, which makes it a real estate marketplace and brokerage serving companies as tenants.

Structured AI sells an AI-powered QA/QC and code-compliance review platform for drawing sets and Revit models to architects and engineers, helping them catch errors before construction and avoid RFIs, change orders, and field rework.

Pickle sells individual consumers a personal AI memory system that learns their context, delivered through a web chat app and its own AI-powered AR glasses (Pickle 1), so it is primarily a consumer hardware device play with a secondary fit in augmented reality.

TagMango sells a SaaS platform that lets Indian edutainment creators set up paid communities and sell exclusive content, courses and services to their audiences, so it fits best as a creator-economy content business with a community (social) component.

Blixo sells accounts receivable automation software, covering invoicing, subscription billing, collections, and cash application, to businesses that want to get paid faster, with payment collection as a secondary element.

Coderhouse sells live online tech courses with AI-assisted feedback directly to individual learners in Latin America and the US, teaching job-ready skills such as AI engineering and data analytics; it also fits the education category under Other.

Ditto Biosciences uses AI to mine parasite-derived immunomodulatory proteins and engineer them into its own autoimmune disease therapies, intended for patients through regulatory approval, with an AI drug discovery platform as a secondary angle.

Moonvalley sells an AI creative studio built on its own video and image foundation models, which lets creators, filmmakers and studios generate visual media; the creation tool fits B2B Productivity and the media output gives it a secondary Consumer Content angle.

trii sells a regulator-compliant retail investing app that lets individual investors in Latin America invest in local markets, so investment platforms for retail investors is the best fit; its brokerage and trading-access role also places it partly in banking and exchange.

Datafold sells AI-powered developer tooling to data engineering teams at companies like Perplexity and Disney, automating code reviews, data testing, and data platform migrations; it also sits close to the data infrastructure layer those teams run on.

AlgoUniversity sells job-focused, year-long live tech training cohorts to Indian college students. Students pay through income-sharing agreements once they land tech jobs, which makes it a consumer career-advancement service with a secondary fit in education.

Poka Labs sells an AI pricing and quoting platform to sales reps at chemical and industrial manufacturers to respond to customer requests and win deals, making it primarily a sales tool with a vertical focus on manufacturing.

ANORIA sells a wearable device directly to individual consumers that reads their emotional state and coaches them to improve emotional intelligence, a self-directed wellness product rather than a clinical one, delivered through consumer hardware.
Simplify sells an AI job-search copilot that helps individual job seekers discover and apply to jobs, and is expanding into recruiter-facing hiring tools for businesses.

Shasta Health sells AI agents to healthcare providers that automate front-office administrative workflows like patient calls and texts, insurance verification, and prior authorizations, which is software for managing operational workflows rather than delivering care.

GiveAway runs a community-driven marketplace where individual consumers give away unneeded household items and other users bid on them with virtual coins, helping people declutter their homes at no cost.

SpotPay sells a stablecoin-based borderless neobank account to individual users for holding, saving, and earning on balances, with payments features like cross-border receiving, local payments, and card spending.

Fresco sells AI-powered takeoff and estimating software to general contractors and Division 8 (doors, frames, and hardware) subcontractors to automate bid preparation for physical construction projects.

Farmtheory runs a farm-to-fork wholesale distribution chain in India, buying cosmetically imperfect produce that farms would otherwise leave unsold and delivering it to restaurants, which makes it primarily a B2B goods-distribution business with a secondary agri-tech angle on the farm side.

Curacel sells AI-powered claims automation and fraud detection infrastructure to insurers, TPAs, and healthcare providers, placing it in insurance technology with a strong healthcare-claims IT component.

Milliray builds high-frequency radar systems that detect and track small and nano drones, selling counter-drone surveillance to front-line defense forces, airports, and critical-infrastructure operators; that makes it a defense and security technology rather than a maker of drones or drone services.

Oda sells an AI interior-design agent that helps homebuyers and renters personalize their new homes and shop for furniture, décor, and appliances, and it reaches them through real estate platforms that embed its AI-designed listing visuals to market properties.

AccioJob sells tech skilling programmes (data analytics, data science, AI engineering) through physical centres and online to Indian graduates, then places them with 500+ hiring partners, making it a consumer career-advancement and job-placement service with a strong education component.

Eze sells businesses an IT asset management platform for tracking, procuring, and reselling or recycling company laptops, phones, and licenses, which is an internal IT operations workflow that also touches physical equipment logistics.

Vobi sells all-in-one project management software to small construction businesses in Latin America, such as remodelers, contractors, and architects, to plan, estimate, procure, and pay suppliers for their building projects.

Rise Reforming sells modular on-site units that thermochemically convert wasted or flared biogas from sites like wastewater plants into low-carbon chemicals and fuels (DME, methanol) for chemical and fuel buyers, which fits climate-focused waste-gas utilization with a secondary fit in fuel production.

Powder sells AI agents to wealth advisory firms that parse brokerage, tax, and estate documents, take meeting notes, and run portfolio analysis to generate personalized sales proposals that help advisors win new clients.

Chari sells a B2B e-commerce ordering and next-day delivery platform for consumer goods to traditional proximity retailers in French-speaking Africa, effectively digitizing wholesale distribution, and also provides microloans to those retailers.

Andi sells individual consumers an ad-free, privacy-focused generative AI search engine that finds, summarizes, and explains information from the web, so its core offering is informational content delivered for reading.

Charm sells a universal peer-to-peer payments app that lets consumers send money to anyone regardless of the app they use, with a secondary interest-bearing balance feature that resembles a deposit account.

Okani sells a low-cost wellness membership directly to uninsured Mexican consumers, providing digital primary care via chat and app and coordinating secondary care with physicians, labs, pharmacies, and clinics, which makes it primarily a care-delivery service with a consumer wellness angle.

Bamboo sells an online brokerage that gives wealthy Africans a mobile app to invest directly in US and global securities, and gives their asset managers a tool to execute trades and manage multiple portfolios, which makes it an investing platform with trading-infrastructure elements.

Algen runs a CRISPR and machine-learning discovery platform that maps disease-driving RNA at single-cell resolution to find first-in-class drugs, which it can partner with pharma companies or advance as its own cancer and inflammation therapeutics.

Kiwi Biosciences develops patent-pending digestive enzymes that break down common food triggers, sold directly to the roughly 18M Americans with IBS so they can eat normal meals without symptoms; its novel enzymes targeting a medical condition also give it a therapeutic angle.

Modulari-T develops synthetic-gene cell therapies that reprogram immune cells to kill cancer, intended for patient treatment. Its cell-engineering platform could also be offered as tooling to other cell-therapy developers.
Cinapse sells production-scheduling software to film and TV production teams, helping them plan, budget, and run shoots, which is a vertical operational workflow tool for entertainment businesses.

Cuanto sells an all-in-one commerce platform to small merchants in Latin America and the developing world, letting them launch storefronts, sell over social media, and manage fulfillment, with built-in payment processing as a core component.

Instalab sells direct-to-consumer preventative health testing and treatments to individuals such as founders, executives, and athletes who want self-directed insight into their health, with a diagnostic-testing component as well.

Liv Labs sells the Pippa Resistance Spring directly to women as a self-directed wellness device for strengthening the pelvic floor during exercise; because it is NIH-funded hardware that interacts with the body to address leakage, it also has a genuine secondary fit as a medical device.

Hazel sells AI software to U.S. federal, state, and local government agencies that automates procurement workflows, from requirements generation and market research through solicitation drafting and proposal evaluation; this is an internal operations tool, and its exclusive government customer base adds a GovTech dimension.

CoArena runs a crowdsourced arena where users pit computer-use AI agents against each other on real tasks, and it sells the resulting evaluations and preference data to AI labs as tooling for testing and improving the agents they build and ship.
Ramen VR is building XR and AI development tools for creators of online games and virtual worlds, and as the studio behind the VR game Zenith it also builds games sold directly to players.

Pluto.markets sells a low-cost, mobile stock-investing product directly to retail investors in non-Euro EU countries, making it a consumer investment platform that also operates brokerage and trading access.

Roofr sells software to roofing contractors for aerial roof measurement reports and proposal/e-signature tools, so it is construction-contractor software that also functions as sales tooling for closing jobs.

Flai sells AI voice assistants to car dealerships that answer calls 24/7, capture leads, book test drives and service appointments, and run outbound recall campaigns, which is sales and customer-handling software built for the automotive retail sector.

Bits to Atoms sells candidate-matching and hiring services to deep technology startups struggling to fill specialized roles, and also serves job seekers by matching them to openings and closing their skill gaps.

T3 Chat sells a general-purpose AI chat app that helps individuals and teams work faster across tasks, alongside developer tools like UploadThing (file uploads for full-stack developers) and creator tools like PicThing and Ping.gg.

Tendo sells a mobile social-commerce platform to African micro-entrepreneurs, letting them resell local wholesalers' products through channels like WhatsApp with no upfront inventory, while handling sourcing, delivery, and payment; it is mainly a merchant commerce tool, with a secondary wholesale-distribution and logistics role.

Careerist sells tech-career training, financing, and automated job-application tools directly to individual job seekers to help them land jobs in QA, sales, and support, with the training side also fitting education.
